stories.label: IRAN
stories.headline: US forces ready to strike Iran within 96 hours of an order
stories.summary: CNN reports US forces can launch a major operation against Iran within 96 hours of a Trump order, with energy, military and nuclear sites as possible targets. Trump has not decided, and any order may come after the November 3 US midterms.

lines.text: Sir, US forces are reported ready to launch a major operation against Iran within ninety-six hours of an order.
Has the President given the order?
Not yet. Trump says an attack is a possibility. Reports say a decision may wait until after the November third midterms.
Possible targets include energy infrastructure, military sites and nuclear facilities.

stories.label: STRAIT OF HORMUZ
stories.headline: Tanker on fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's army says an oil tanker caught fire after hitting naval mines on a route Tehran had not authorised, with its tracking switched off. Iran says the strait is closed to ships that don't follow its rules, and its foreign minister says it will not return to pre-war arrangements.

lines.text: An oil tanker is on fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines.
Whose mines?
Iran's army says the ship used a route Tehran had not authorised, with its tracking systems switched off.
Iran now says the strait is completely closed to vessels that don't follow Iranian rules, and will not go back to pre-war arrangements.

stories.label: SAUDI ARABIA
stories.headline: Houthi missiles intercepted over Riyadh
stories.summary: Saudi air defences destroyed two ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh by Yemen's Houthis; shrapnel caused material damage. Saudi forces also downed three drones and say they destroyed two launchers in Sanaa. The Houthis claim they hit Riyadh's airport and oil pumping stations.

lines.text: Sir, two Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted over Riyadh.
Any damage?
Shrapnel caused material damage. Saudi forces also shot down three drones and destroyed two launchers in Sanaa.
The Houthis claim they hit Riyadh airport and oil pumping stations. Those claims are not confirmed.

stories.label: EGYPT
stories.headline: Egypt authorises military support for Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Egypt's parliament approved military support for Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. A Houthi political bureau member said the move amounts to a declaration of war against Yemen.

lines.text: Egypt's parliament has authorised military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.
Egypt is joining the fight?
It is authorised, not yet deployed. The Houthis call it a declaration of war against Yemen.

stories.label: PAKISTAN
stories.headline: Pakistan army chief joins peace talks in Tehran
stories.summary: Pakistan's army chief, Saudi Arabia's defence minister and Turkey's intelligence chief met Iranian officials in Tehran under the Mecca Common Defence Agreement. All sides agreed to keep talking. Saudi Arabia's cabinet reviewed the talks on Tuesday.

lines.text: Pakistan's army chief has held talks in Tehran with Saudi and Turkish officials.
Any result?
All four countries agreed to keep talking. Iran says security should come from inside the region, not from foreign forces.
Oil prices eased on the news.

stories.label: GLOBAL MARKETS
stories.headline: Oil slips to about $115 as Gulf diplomacy picks up
stories.summary: Brent fell about $1 to $114.81 a barrel and WTI to $100.98 after the Tehran talks. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia limited the drop. UBS expects Brent to stay near $110 through year-end.

lines.text: Markets update. Brent crude is down about one dollar, near one hundred and fifteen dollars a barrel.
Why the drop?
The Tehran talks eased supply fears. But attacks on Saudi Arabia kept prices high. UBS expects Brent near one hundred and ten dollars until year end.

stories.label: ISRAEL
stories.headline: Record turnout in Israel's election
stories.summary: Turnout hit 44.9% by 2pm, the highest since 1973, in the first election since October 7, 2023. Netanyahu is in a tight race. Defence Minister Katz said there would be no attack on Iran before the vote.

lines.text: Israel's election has record turnout. Forty-four point nine percent by two p.m., the highest since 1973.
Who's leading?
Netanyahu is in a tight race. His defence minister says there will be no attack on Iran before the vote.

stories.label: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES
stories.headline: UAE flights to Saudi Arabia disrupted; Europe routes returning
stories.summary: Etihad extended cancellations on Abu Dhabi–Saudi flights until November 5. Emirates, flydubai and Air Arabia list cancellations on Saudi routes. UAE departing seats rose 23% to 7.2 million from June to October, and up to 36 weekly Dubai–Europe flights should return by December.

lines.text: UAE travel update. Etihad has cancelled Abu Dhabi to Saudi flights until November fifth.
What about Dubai?
Emirates, flydubai and Air Arabia also list cancellations on Saudi routes. Check your flight before you travel.
Good news: up to thirty-six weekly Dubai to Europe flights should be back by December.

stories.label: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES
stories.headline: UAE President honours flydubai crew; Flag Day call
stories.summary: The UAE President awarded the flydubai crew the Order of Zayed II for their courage during the September 30 mid-air attack. Sheikh Mohammed called on the public to raise the flag for Flag Day.

lines.text: The UAE President has honoured the flydubai crew for their courage during the September thirtieth mid-air attack.
They received the Order of Zayed the Second. Sheikh Mohammed has also called on everyone to raise the flag for Flag Day.

stories.label: PAKISTAN
stories.headline: Pakistan LPG prices rise as Iran border stays shut
stories.summary: Pakistan's petroleum minister blamed the closed Pakistan–Iran border for higher LPG prices and said the government is sourcing fuel by sea. The State Bank's rate hike has split business: investors back it, industry warns it will hurt exports.

lines.text: Pakistan. LPG prices are rising because the border with Iran is closed.
What is the government doing?
It is trying to bring fuel in by sea. Meanwhile the State Bank's interest rate hike has split the business community.

stories.label: KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA
stories.headline: Peshawar operation against illegal Afghan residents from Nov 1
stories.summary: Authorities plan an operation against illegal Afghan residents in Peshawar from November 1 using 120 special teams. In KP, the PTI called off a protest after an emergency was imposed. Gatherings are banned in Pishin, Balochistan, ahead of an operation.

lines.text: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Peshawar will start an operation against illegal Afghan residents on November first.
How big?
One hundred and twenty special teams. The PTI also called off its protest in KP after the emergency was imposed.

stories.label: OMAN
stories.headline: Oman proposes Gulf security pact that includes Iran
stories.summary: Oman's foreign minister proposed a Gulf security framework including Iran and a non-aggression pact among eight states. Iran's president met Qatar's emir in Moscow, and an Iranian official set seven conditions for new talks with Washington.

lines.text: Oman has proposed a Gulf security pact that includes Iran.
Is Iran interested?
Iran's president met Qatar's emir in Moscow. But Tehran has set seven conditions before any new talks with Washington.

stories.label: IRAQ
stories.headline: Ship on fire off Iraq's Al-Faw
stories.summary: UKMTO reports a vessel caught fire about 63 nautical miles southeast of Al-Faw, Iraq. Crew status and damage are unknown.

lines.text: A second vessel is on fire, sixty-three nautical miles southeast of Al-Faw, Iraq.
The crew?
Unknown for now. The British maritime agency UKMTO is monitoring.

stories.label: UNITED KINGDOM
stories.headline: Two charged over plot at UK airbase used by US
stories.summary: UK counter-terrorism police charged two British men over an incident last month at an airbase used by the United States. One is charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service believed linked to Iran.

lines.text: Britain has charged two men over an incident at an airbase used by US forces.
One is accused of helping a foreign intelligence service believed to be linked to Iran.

stories.label: SOUTH KOREA
stories.headline: Cold wave hits South Korea; Seoul village fire put out
stories.summary: Cold wave advisories cover most of South Korea, with some regions below freezing. A fire in Seoul's Guryong Village burned for 13 hours; all residents got out safely. The US said wartime operational control will transfer when agreed conditions are met.

lines.text: South Korea. A cold wave has hit, with Seoul at its coldest morning of the autumn.
A large fire in Seoul's Guryong Village burned for thirteen hours. All residents evacuated safely.
